title: Rule identifiability in elementary cellular automata under dynamical noise
description: Exact computation (no sampling, no seeds) of rule identifiability in elementary cellular automata under dynamical bit-flip noise. On a ring of 12 cells: zero-noise consistency classes for all 256 rules x 4096 initial states, the identifiability rate rho(f; eps) = lambda(eps) min_c nu_c(f; eps) for all 88 rule classes on a noise grid with the best noise level eps* per class, finite-horizon evidence margins from every initial state, and a boundary check with radius-2 generators. Version 0.2 adds the exact small-noise theory: the noise-selected cycles (minimum stochastic potential), the orders k_c and k* of the stationary neighbourhood frequencies and the asymptotics rho ~ a eps^k* log(1/eps), computed in integer arithmetic for all 88 classes at n = 12 and for ring sizes n = 4..20 (checked certificates for n = 12 and n <= 14). This settles the classes that version 0.1 left to a numerical trend and corrects class 106. Version 0.3 adds a study of the 13 classes whose small-noise order k* changes side with the ring size (report_ring_size.md): the mechanisms, computed for n <= 22 (in ten of the classes a spatially periodic crystal that exists only when its period divides n, or a zero state that cannot be left by one flip), and two statements proved for all n by the independent verification session: for rule 154, k* = 1 if and only if n is a power of two (n >= 3); for class 94, k* = 1 at every n >= 6 divisible by 3. These proofs are not peer reviewed. Version 0.4 adds a paper, paper/ring_size_paper.pdf (Noise-selected cycles of elementary cellular automata and the arithmetic of the ring size; also archived as a record of its own, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24482169), with proofs for all ring sizes from a small bound on: k* = 1 if and only if n is a power of two for rule 154 (n >= 3), if and only if 4 divides n for rules 43 and 142 (n >= 4); for rule 94, k* = 1 if 3 divides n (n >= 6) and k* = 0 otherwise (n >= 5); for rule 26 on 2^k cells the zero state is the only noise-selected cycle. Each proof document and the paper were verified by a separate session; none of this is peer reviewed. Version 0.5 adds no mathematics: it contains version 2 of the paper, in which the corrections made after its verification were checked by a further session and one source cited as not read (Young 1993) was read. Version 0.6 adds a study of the same question on a row with null walls and with reflecting walls instead of a ring (report_boundaries.md): computed for rows up to 20 cells, proved for the additive rules 60, 90 and 150; verified by a separate session. The note itself is unchanged (version 0.2). Includes code, data files with a SHA-256 manifest, the note as PDF, and the reports of the independent verification sessions.
